question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Honestly the cost of everything. Tuition is one thing but books and parking add up fast. More emergency grant options would really help.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Making friends has been harder than I expected. Everyone seems to already have their group. More low-pressure social events early in the semester would help.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Balancing my job with classes. I work 25 hours a week and some professors act like their class is the only thing in my life. Recorded lectures would help a lot.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: The jump in workload from high school. I never learned how to study properly. A required study skills workshop in the first month would have saved me.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Commuting. I spend almost three hours a day on the train and miss most evening events. More things scheduled between classes instead of at night.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: I got really homesick in October and my grades slipped. Talking to counseling helped but the wait was three weeks. Shorter wait times for counseling please.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Registration was confusing and I ended up in a class I did not need. Clearer degree maps and more advisor availability during registration week.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Math. Just math. The tutoring center is good but it gets packed before exams. More tutors during midterms and finals.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Feeling like I belong here. I am the first in my family to go to college and sometimes I feel like everyone else got a handbook I did not. The first-gen mentoring program has been great, more of that.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Time management. Between classes, my shift at the bookstore, and family stuff I am always behind. A planning workshop or an app the school actually supports.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Nothing major honestly. It has gone better than I expected.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Financial aid paperwork. My package changed mid-semester and nobody could explain why. One person who owns your case instead of a different email every time.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: The dining options close too early for people with night classes. Keep at least one place open until 9.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: My roommate situation was rough and it affected everything else. Faster response from residence life when there is a real conflict.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Speaking up in class. I get anxious in discussions even when I know the answer. Smaller discussion sections would make it easier.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Figuring out what I actually want to major in. Career services was helpful once I found it, but nobody points you there in first year.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: The cost of the meal plan compared to what you get. Let commuters opt out completely.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Chemistry lab reports. The expectations were never explained, just graded. Example reports or a rubric up front.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: I am on my phone too much and my focus is shot. This one is on me, but phone-free study rooms in the library might actually help.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Missing my family. Video calls help. The international student office events made a big difference for me, more weekend ones please.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Professors who only use email versus ones who only use the portal versus ones who use neither. Pick one system for the whole school.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Textbook costs. Two hundred dollars for a book we used twice. Put required readings on library reserve.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Everything moves so fast. By the time I realized I was failing statistics the drop deadline had passed. Midterm grade alerts that actually reach students.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Parking. I have been late to my 8am twice circling the garage. Either more spots or stop scheduling 8am classes.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: I joined the outdoors club and it changed my whole experience. My challenge was the first two months before that. Push clubs harder at orientation.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Writing papers at the college level. The writing center booked out fast. More drop-in hours would help.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: My anxiety got worse with all the change. The counseling group sessions helped once I got in. Advertise them better, I found out by accident.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Being older than everyone in my classes. As a transfer veteran student the orientation stuff did not fit me at all. A separate track for adult learners.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Not sure yet honestly, still figuring it out.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Wifi in the residence halls drops constantly during evening hours which is exactly when everything is due. Fix the wifi.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Understanding my bill. Fees appear with names that mean nothing. A bill in plain English.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Loneliness on weekends when the campus empties out. More weekend programming for the students who stay.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Keeping my scholarship GPA while working. The pressure is constant. Maybe scholarship students could get priority registration so we can build workable schedules.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Group projects where nobody else does the work. Let us rate our group members and have it count.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Honestly just adjusting to living away from home, cooking, laundry, all of it. A basic life skills workshop would be funny but useful.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: The advising office keeps 9 to 5 hours and I have class or work during all of them. Evening or virtual advising appointments.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: I failed my first exam ever and spiraled for a while. My professor noticed and reached out, which honestly saved my semester. Train more faculty to do that.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Public speaking requirement terrifies me. Smaller sections or an alternative format option.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: Not knowing what resources exist until it is too late. One page that lists everything: tutoring, counseling, food pantry, emergency funds. Put it on the back of every syllabus.

question_text: What has been the most challenging part of your first year, and what would help you succeed?
response_text: It has mostly been good. My advisor is great and the small classes are why I chose this school. Keep class sizes small.
